summary: The bots trained for 3 rounds: 14208 air-only matches, 2 against 2, 6 game-minutes each. A change was kept only when it won by more than luck.

Bf 109 G-6: kept its tactics: nothing tried beat the noise. Now it turn-fights, never breaks off, throttles back in turns. Kills per life 0.25 before, 0.25 after; own crashes and collisions 0.08 per life before, 0.09 after.

Spitfire Mk IX: kept its tactics: nothing tried beat the noise. Now it turn-fights, never breaks off, opens fire at 115% of the usual range, throttles back in turns. Kills per life 1.01 before, 0.98 after; own crashes and collisions 0.1 per life before, 0.09 after.

P-47D Thunderbolt: learned to change firing range (1.15 → 1.3). Now it turn-fights, never breaks off, opens fire at 130% of the usual range, throttles back in turns. Kills per life 0.42 before, 0.51 after; own crashes and collisions 0.07 per life before, 0.09 after.

La-5FN: kept its tactics: nothing tried beat the noise. Now it turn-fights, never breaks off, throttles back in turns. Kills per life 0.41 before, 0.39 after; own crashes and collisions 0.1 per life before, 0.1 after.

Ki-43-II Hayabusa: kept its tactics: nothing tried beat the noise. Now it turn-fights, never breaks off, throttles back in turns. Kills per life 0.17 before, 0.17 after; own crashes and collisions 0.08 per life before, 0.08 after.

Brewster B-239: kept its tactics: nothing tried beat the noise. Now it turn-fights, never breaks off, opens fire at 115% of the usual range, throttles back in turns. Kills per life 1.04 before, 1.03 after; own crashes and collisions 0.11 per life before, 0.11 after.
The kills-per-life numbers are from a short check (every pairing, a few matches), so small changes there can be luck. The Balance Lab run started next shows the effect on the real battle.
